_doc: Random worlds (ADR-0031, docs/REGIONS.md 'Random worlds'). `options` are the settings the New Game screen's World tab shows (type int/float/enum, range or values, default, category, label), `presets` override their defaults, and a world is a pure function of (seed, resolved settings, RwgGenerator.VERSION). `tuning` holds the generator's numbers; `names` the place names it draws from. Read through WorldGenSettings (typed; unknown keys are errors, checked by `make validate`).

standard.label: Standard
standard.description: Rolling forest country, a few rivers and lakes, three towns of mixed size and the usual camps, cabins and lookouts between them.

small_valley.label: Small valley (3 x 3)
small_valley.description: A 3 km valley with two villages: quick to generate and to cross.

highlands.label: Highlands
highlands.description: Mountain ranges and deep valleys, bare rock above the trees, few lakes and two small settlements on the valley floors.

lakeland.label: Lakeland
lakeland.description: Low rolling country full of lakes and slow rivers, birch along the water.

settled.label: Settled county
settled.description: More towns and bigger ones, open farmland and a dense road net: more to loot, more of them.

wild.label: Wild country
wild.description: One hamlet, a few tracks and a lot of forest between the camps.

tuning._doc: Generator numbers. Lengths in metres. See RwgGenerator / RwgTerrain / RwgTowns.

terrain._doc: Per terrain setting: base height, relief of the rolling noise, ridge (mountain range) strength, valley carving and the map's tilt (what drains rivers off one edge), all in metres or factors.

rivers._doc: catchment: km² a river must drain at its mouth (a tributary 0.6 of that where it joins); head: km² where a traced river starts; count: most rivers per km² of map (none/few/some/many).

lakes._doc: per_region: expected lakes per region; radius range of the basin.

towns._doc: Organic towns (ADR-0040; the planner's own tuning is data/config/town_planner.json). How many towns: the town_density option (towns per 16 km²); their size classes: mix (weights by town_size). Sites (plan §3.3): candidates per town, each disc `spacing` m clear of every other town's and `edge` m inside the map; the centre `water` [0] m from water at least, [1]-[2] m a bonus; core and disc relief at most core_relief and disc_relief m, the disc's mean slope at most max_slope by class (else the least steep disc found, a little more); score: slope (core mean slope), disc_slope (the disc's), valley (per m above the 1 km mean), water (bonus), central (to the map's middle), edge (per m closer than 300 m to the edge), jitter. core_smoothing: how far the macro grid eases towards its mean over the core. stub: how far past its radius a lone main street runs. authored_max: towns of one world that may hold each authored building. clearance: what places keep off lots and streets (m).

roads._doc: Road classes and the network: extra: loops added beyond the spanning tree per density (per 16 km²); exits: roads off the map per density (per 4 km of map side); grade: preferred and steepest grades; costs are relative; valley: extra cost per metre of road per metre above the ground's 300 m mean (roads keep to the valleys).

wilderness._doc: Authored places outside towns. site: summit | forest | waterside | lake_shore | remote | roadside | mine (pad: the levelled surface part [w, d] of a footprint that runs on under a hill; see `mine`); per_region: expected count per region at density 1; max: per 16 km² of map; access: trail (footpath) | track (dirt road) | drive (short asphalt drive off the road); min_danger: 1 (start) .. 5 (far edge). unique: true caps the entry at one per world whatever its size (a place the story knows as one). door: where the access ends, in footprint metres (default 3 m before the middle of the front).

mine._doc: `mine` sites (TD-169): a POI with buried levels dug into a hillside, its pad (the pool entry's `pad`, footprint metres from its origin) at the foot and the levels running uphill under the ground. slope: the least macro slope where the levels go in; cover: metres of reference ground over every buried ceiling `taper` m beyond the pad, `portal` m at its edge (a drift comes out of the hill there; the region's detail noise takes some of it); pad_relief: the most the ground may vary over the pad; approach: how far out along the contour from the door its track arrives; road: the farthest a site may be from a highway, county road or track (so a track can reach it).

drop_site._doc: Where a new player lands: away from towns and places, near (not on) a road, on gentle dry ground, `border` m from a region border (the first that has room).

bloom._doc: Bloom patches (ADR-0025) in the far regions: per region at danger 3, 4 and 5.

burn._doc: Fire scars (ADR-0041): fires per 16 km² at burn 1.0 (x the burn option); each spreads over this many 64 m biome cells (low end more likely), no scar past max_share of the map's cells and all of them past twice that; water within `water` m, roads within `road` m, fens, towns (+ town_clear) and the drop site (drop_clear) stop it; islands: noise level above which a cell the fire reached stays green.

fen._doc: Fens (ADR-0041): on ground flatter than max_slope, within `water` m of a river or lake, low on the map (elevation fraction `low`, raised by the fen option) or `valley` m under the ground 400 m round, in patches of noise about `patch` m across; town_clear / drop_clear keep them off towns and the start. pools: per fen cell the chance of pools, how many, their radius, depth under the edge drop (wading depth), how far the water stands under the ground round it (drop), shore width, outline irregularity, the slope they need and how far they keep inside a region border.
